parts.name: The two declared indices, and which side of the boundary the skill's text sits on
parts.statement: Before any claim in this slice about what an agent owns, retains or loses, two indices are declared and not discovered. The boundary: the system is the reader together with the program that builds and hands it its context; the record, the corpus and the owner are outside it. The continuity: what persists from one execution to the next, which differs by arm (the agent's process and transcript in arm (a); the carrier text the rig hands over in arms (b), (c), (c'); the document and the frozen question in arm (d)). Added here: the skill's text once it is in the context is inside the boundary, and the work of writing that text is outside it.

parts.name: Stateful and stateless, as a construction on the constructor attribute
parts.statement: A stateful agent is one whose constructor attribute between calls is the set of states carrying the represented targets of its unfinished work. A stateless agent's attribute between calls is only what its carrier text carries. The pair is a construction: file 11 has attributes, retained realization, the retention fixed point and owned capability, and contains neither word.

The transport's provenance is declared when the designer wrote the lookup, and constructed when the agent built the query from a difficulty it represents. It bears on attention by deciding which targets are represented at the next call. Saying a store is the agent's memory does not make its contents represented.

parts.name: A harness that sets a port the organization's components assign replaces that component
parts.statement: A harness that writes tokens into the emission, or fixes its shape — a prefilled report skeleton, a closed list the marks must come from — sets ports that the organization's own components assign. Each such edit replaces the component, so the set port takes the harness's value and the other ports in that component's footprint lose the relation it imposed on them; a deleted component imposes the full relation on its ports, which is no constraint at all. That loss is what the harness costs. A harness that only adds passages to the context sets no such port: it is a change to what the call reads, and the model predicts no within-step loss from it.

rests_on.quote: A deleted component imposes the full relation on its ports. An edit that sets a port replaces the component assigning that port; it does not add an equation beside an incompatible one.

rests_on.quote: A port \(v\) is an **input** under \(A\) when \(A\) contains an edit that sets \(v\) directly.

word_list.plain_word: the line drawn round the system
word_list.part_heading: Part XII — The physical module, "System boundary and continuity"
word_list.quote: A capability is attributed to a system under a declared boundary (which processes and resources are the system's) and a declared continuity \(\Omega\) (what makes it the same system through change).
word_list.meaning: Which processes and resources count as the system's, said before any claim about what it can do.

word_list.plain_word: what makes it the same system through change
word_list.part_heading: Part XII — The physical module, "System boundary and continuity"
word_list.quote: A replaced part that preserves the declared continuity leaves the same system; a process run inside the boundary is the system's whoever wrote it; a process run outside it is not the system's however close it sits.
word_list.meaning: What has to persist for this to count as the same system from one execution to the next.

word_list.plain_word: an input the model must state and cannot supply
word_list.part_heading: Part XIV — The class collected, "Declared inputs"
word_list.quote: A verdict that depends on one of these is a verdict given the input; where the input is missing, the verdict is unsettled and the semantics says so rather than choosing the input from the verdict wanted.
word_list.meaning: Where a claim rests on something stated rather than derived, the claim holds only given that statement.

word_list.plain_word: an index, not a fact about the world
word_list.part_heading: Part XIV — The class collected, "Indices, not primitives"
word_list.quote: Grain \(\ell\), boundary \(\beta\), continuity \(\Omega\), and the contract \(C\) are declared indices. Every claim is relative to them; none is a predicate that could be true or false.
word_list.meaning: Four things every claim is relative to, which no test can confirm or refute.

word_list.plain_word: a set of states the system can be in
word_list.part_heading: Part XII — The physical module, "Tasks"
word_list.quote: A substrate is a physical system; an attribute a set of its states; a task a permitted input-to-output attribute transformation with explicit resources and side effects.
word_list.meaning: The physical module's unit for "the system is in one of these states".

word_list.plain_word: the work finishes and leaves the system able to do it again
word_list.part_heading: Part XII — The physical module, "Retained realization"
word_list.quote: Execution families are nonempty on legitimate inputs; deadlock is not vacuous success.
word_list.meaning: Every execution from a constructor state completes with a permitted output and returns the system into the constructor attribute.

word_list.plain_word: which states keep that property
word_list.part_heading: Part XII — The physical module, "Retention fixed point"
word_list.quote: \(F(C)\) = states whose executions all complete and return into \(C\).
word_list.meaning: The largest set of states from which the work can be done and done again; it says nothing about what those states carry.

word_list.plain_word: what the system itself can do
word_list.part_heading: Part XII — The physical module, "Owned capability"
word_list.quote: \(\operatorname{Can}_{\Omega,\beta}(\xi,T;\chi)\) requires an owned retained realization or an owned, physically admitted, finite construction of one under the same continuity and resource contract.
word_list.meaning: A capability attributed to a system under its declared boundary, continuity and resources; the reading this model gives the owner's "latent capability".

word_list.plain_word: owning is not read off what it can do
word_list.term: ownership (Part XII), and the well-founded order (Part XIV)
word_list.part_heading: Part XII — The physical module, "Owned capability"
word_list.quote: Ownership is grounded in the processes and resources the boundary includes, never in the capability being attributed: "owned because it can, and can because owned" grounds neither.
word_list.meaning: What makes a process the system's own is where the boundary falls, not the capability the attribution is for.

word_list.plain_word: stateful and stateless
word_list.term: the constructor attribute between calls (a construction on CT1, CT2, Part XII's attribute and Part IV's represented target)
word_list.part_heading: Part XII — The physical module (Tasks, Retained realization, Retention fixed point, Owned capability); Part IV — Layers, transports, and provenance (Three provenances, Constructed)
word_list.quote: There is an episode (Part X) whose construction witness prepares \(t\), and in which \(t\), or the organization it targets, is available as a represented target.
word_list.meaning: Stateful: the attribute between calls carries the represented targets of unfinished work. Stateless: the attribute between calls is only what the carrier text carries. Neither word is in file 11.

word_list.plain_word: a physically located carrier
word_list.part_heading: Part IV — Layers, transports, and provenance, "Occurrences and contents"
word_list.quote: An **occurrence** is a physically located carrier.
word_list.meaning: A thing in the world that bears text; a file, a prompt, a reply.

word_list.plain_word: saying so does not make it so
word_list.part_heading: Part IV — Layers, transports, and provenance, "Representation is derived"
word_list.quote: A declared transport does not make an occurrence represent anything; it makes a modeller assert that it does.
word_list.meaning: A lookup the designer wrote carries text in; it does not thereby make the text represented by the system.

word_list.plain_word: a lookup the designer wrote, against a query the agent built
word_list.term: external memory (a construction on Part IV's three provenances and Part IX's active route)
word_list.part_heading: Part IV — Layers, transports, and provenance, "Three provenances"; Part IX — Criticism, use, and standing, "Histories"
word_list.quote: A route that started and did no work, or that was already at rest when the result occurred, is not active for that result; whether a route is active is read from the history, not from the result.

word_list.plain_word: a copy is not a second witness

report:
## The question, frozen

Which of the theory's objects an agent built on a large language model instantiates at one call, which across calls, which only with a record or a harness, and which never — this slice takes the arrangement: retention, ownership, boundary and continuity, stateful and stateless, what the context must carry, external memory and its carriers, and the two losses under a harness. The grain is text: what is in the context, what is emitted, and what changes in the emission when the context is changed. Range: the agent kinds this record has run. The model claims no class membership, no creativity, no knowledge, no Deploy for any agent.

## Parts and jobs

Four jobs are the owner's, quoted in the jobs table: Q2 (stateful against stateless), Q3 (what the context must carry), Q4 (external memory), and the emission half of Q1 (the harness). Four are mine and tagged so: every ownership claim carries the two declared indices; every part names the arm that could falsify it or says none does; the field sorting is written before any run; the two harness losses stay apart.

Twelve parts, B1 to B12. Two are constructions and say so with the passages they are built from (B2, stateful/stateless; B5's requirement on a call's context; and the external-memory row of the word list). One is borrowed and names its rival (B11's attention half). One is unknown with the test named (B10). The rest are held or held if, each with a quoted holder.

## Part by part

| Part | Mark | Held by | Provenance |
|---|---|---|---|
| B1 the two declared indices, and the skill's text inside the boundary | held | Part XIV's \"where the input is missing, the verdict is unsettled\", with my added job | asserted |
| B2 stateful/stateless as the constructor attribute | held if (P4.1, P4.2, certified fields) | Part XII's grounding sentence, which stops the pair being defined by what it predicts | built |
| B3 the difference tracks what is represented, not the label | held, jointly with slice A's M3 | Derivation 2's consequence, with Derivation 9 | built |
| B4 the within-step / cross-step sorting | held if (P4.2, P4.3) | Part VI on supports actually written, plus file 54's single-call cross-step findings | built |
| B5 the context must carry the frozen question and the parts | held if (my added job; P4.5 on arm (f)) | Part III's prohibition, plus H62's two question-drifts | built |
| B6 a target may come from the weights | held if (slice A's M2) | file 54's Recall paragraph and H62's four OUTSIDE flags; Part X's first-representation sentence | built |
| B7 external memory by a transport with a provenance | held if (my added job; P-B7) | Part IV's declared-transport sentence; twelve of twelve mode-2 runs opened a module | built |
| B8 a derived record is not a second witness | held if (my added job) | Part IX's reconstructed-record sentence; Part IV's second-witness sentence | built |
| B9 a carry-over note keeps the writing call's history | held if (P4.5 on arm (c')) | Part VIII's patched-section sentence | built |
| B10 a harness that sets a port replaces the component | unknown, until arm (e) runs | nothing yet; arm (e) named as the test | built |
| B11 \"latent capability\" is owned capability; no barrier | borrowed (attention half, from the physical module; rival named) | Part XII's Can and Part XIII's barrier sentence | built |
| B12 partition loses what no call's context holds together | held if (P4.3, restricted) | Part VI's criticality sentence | built |

Never added up. One part with no holder is one part unheld: B10 is that part, and it is named rather than filled in.

## Whole-explanation checks, by their Step 5 names

**Flip.** Run part by part. It does not apply to B1 (a declared index is not a predicate) or to B3 (Derivation 2 is derived, so a condition is dropped instead).

**Reverse.** The claimed cause is what a call's context carries; the effect is which fields appear in the report. Poke the cause: withhold the parts list, the change list or the other parts (arms c, d, f) and fields should drop. Poke the effect: re-mark the same reports with a second marker and nothing about what any call was handed changes. The record has the second half already — H64's blind second marking moved marks across ninety-six reports without touching a run.

**Hunt the answer in the starting points.** The danger is that \"what the context carries\" is the conclusion under another name: the agent does what it was given. The check the theory asks for is a change that removes a working part and moves the answer. Arm (b) supplies it: the whole transcript is handed over and the model predicts *no* loss. A slice that merely said \"what you give it is what you get\" would have to predict a loss there too. The residue is B4: a sorting of fields could be read off the reports afterwards, which is why it is written now and why W3 section 8 forbids re-sorting on the reports that break it.

**Add a job.** The job I added — every part names its arm — ruled out one rival immediately: defining stateful and stateless by the framework's label has no arm, because it makes arm (a) and arm (b) different by definition. That is a job that killed a version, not one that counted.

**Look inside.** Cannot bite here, and I name it rather than leave it out. The model claims what changes in emissions when contexts change; two arrangements built differently inside with the same projection are not separated, by Derivation 9. The parts it would have settled — what any arrangement instantiates — are left unknown at this grain, as W3 section 3 already says.

**Pairs that pull.** Three. (i) B1 against B10/B11: the wider the boundary, the more of the harness's edits are the system's own; the line is drawn first and the harness read under it, and what would show the line wrong is an arm whose result can only be read by moving the line afterwards. (ii) B4 against B12: the more fields called cross-step, the more arm (d) is predicted to lose, and the easier it is for P4.3 to pass for a reason other than partition; the line is drawn at fields phase 3 certified whose object is the set of parts. (iii) B5 against B7: the more the model requires in the context, the less work external memory does; the line is drawn at the frozen question and the construction target, and arm (f) is what would show it in the wrong place.

**Check the patches.** The sketch was patched twice before me: M8 split into two arms after W2 (an arm added, not a bin), and M2's consequence narrowed by file 11 with what it gives up recorded in W5. My own two patches are in the dropped list with the quotations that forced them: B4 restated, B12 restricted. The slice has one catch-all, the operations table's column \"only with a record or a harness\"; its gauge is the tool audit and the modules-opened trace — an operation placed there that appears in an arm with neither is the bin swallowing a job.

**What the change list leaves out.** Anything at the grain of weights or activations. Anything about runs longer than an arm. Any arrangement with more than one reader in it. Whether a provider retains anything server-side that changes an emission (claimed to be nothing; not seen).

**Rivals.** Named per part. The strongest whole-slice rival: *the arrangement is a matter of how much context, not of what it carries.* The change that separates them is the equal-length summary control for arm (c).

**Where the parts came from.** One asserted (B1's line), ten built, none fitted. The one part I would have marked fitted — a sorting read off past reports — is the one I refused to take from the reports and wrote before the run.

## What would make it harder to vary

Two things, in order. First, the equal-length summary control on arm (c): without it, a loss under (c) is compatible with the rival that only length matters, and B4 would be confirmed on a change it never risked. Second, splitting the parts and not only the tests in arm (d): as specified, that arm cannot bear on B12 at all, and a pass or a failure would teach nothing about partition.

## What this does not show

Hard to vary is not true. Nothing here has been tested: no reader ran under any arm, and every piece of evidence I cite was read before this slice was written and cannot confirm a part fitted on it. Four of the citations are claimed, not seen — they are documents about language models read on the web today, quoted with their addresses, and a part resting on one is held if that source is right. Agreement between arms, when it comes, will settle nothing about what any arrangement instantiates.

## One next step

Write the phase-4 arm designs for (c) and (d) to the two shapes named above — an equal-length summary that omits the parts list, and a partition that splits the parts rather than the tests — before the phase-4 plan is frozen, since after freezing they cannot be changed without a new claim.
